newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta Fed - Southeast manufacturing moderating.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta Fed - Southeast manufacturing moderating.

text.p: The Southeast U.S. manufacturing sector shows signs of slower growth but still appears healthy, said Mark Rogers, an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.

"Basically, the Southeast manufacturing sector looks moderate (and) healthy in terms of current activity," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "The data, however, are basically raising a few concerns about possible price pressures."
Inflation concerns largely stem from increased wage costs and signs of rising materials prices, Rogers said.
Nationally, firms have so far offset the earnings loss related to higher costs by boosting productivity, he said.
"U.S. firms have been very creative in terms of keeping costs down (by) gaining productivity when labor costs are rising mildly," Rogers explained.
Looking ahead, the economist said the Atlanta Fed's monthly index suggests manufacturers expect slower growth in the near term.
"They are anticipating moderation and at the same time, keeping their inventories lean, keeping their costs down," he said. "But there's really no sign of any significant weakening."
The Southeast manufacturing sector "appears to be in good shape," he added.
On Monday, the Atlanta Fed said its index of Southeast manufacturing activity rose to 10.3 in March versus a revised 7.1 in February.
